text:
"Worst probable" pollution concentrations are normally calculated based on projected ADT for the time of completion (TOC) of the project and the design year (usually 20 years after the proposed time of completion). Wind and stability data used for these calculations are based on studies of all available wind rose/stability data for the State of Illinois and adjacent locations using Pasquille Stability Class F (most stable) and a wind speed of one meter per second (2.2 mph). This wind speed is suggested by the Federal Environmental Protection Agency as representative for "most stable" conditions. Wind direction for "worst probable" calculations has been assumed as being twenty-two and one-half (22.5) degrees to the project alignment based on the observation that this angular wind condition provides the most pessimistic results for computed pollutant concentrations.
For most Illinois Department of Transportation projects (exclusive of urban/industrialized areas), receptors will not normally be closer than 100 feet to the edge of the project (shoulder of road or curb). Since pollution (other than during episodes) disperses downwind, it is assumed that if the 100-foot distant receptor meets all requirements of national standards, receptors at greater distances than 100 feet will also not receive significant CO concentrations. In the event receptors are located closer than 100 feet to the outside edge of the project, the closer distance is used for calculation of pollutant concentrations.
Air quality calculations for any project are time consuming and expensive. It is reasonable, in the public interest, to restrict calculations to the minimum required to adequately portray the significant air quality impact of the project. Therefore, calculations have been restricted to maximum concentrations. The air quality impact of the carbon monoxide concentrations are not considered to be a severe impact since they are far below the standards established by the Federal Environmental Protection Agency and those of the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency. Air pollution resulting from this project was determined to not be significant based on guidance obtained from Illinois Environmental Protection Agency, and in accordance with proposed FHWA PPM 90-7 relating to precoordination and review procedures.
The pollution concentrations of carbon monoxide (CO) and associated traffic data for the proposed improvement was calculated for two (2) segments because of the differences in the projected ADT and the distance to the nearest receptors.
